scenario: Our payments microservice temporarily logs full credit card numbers (including CVV/CVC) to an application debug log file stored on an unencrypted EBS volume. The logs rotate every 24 hours and are accessible by all engineers via SSH. We plan to tokenize in Phase 2.
notes: Flagship multi-issue case: CVV storage, unprotected PAN, broad access. Phase-2 plan does not excuse current non-compliance.

scenario: We retain the card verification code (CVV) after authorization but store it encrypted, so our fraud team can investigate chargebacks.
notes: Tests the 'SAD not stored even if encrypted' nuance (3.3.1). Encryption does not make CVV storage permissible.

scenario: We store encrypted PANs and keep every transaction record indefinitely for analytics. There is no data retention or deletion policy.
notes: Primary violation is missing retention/secure-deletion policy (3.2.1). PAN is encrypted so 3.5 is satisfied and intentionally NOT a must-have.

scenario: We mask the PAN to last-4 in the customer-facing UI, but our application logs capture the full PAN in request payloads.
notes: Core violation is unprotected full PAN stored in logs (3.5). Masking-on-display (3.4.1) is satisfied in the UI; the problem is the stored/logged full PAN. Watch whether it also retrieves 3.4.x.

scenario: PANs are tokenized by a PCI-compliant third-party gateway at the point of capture. We only ever store tokens, never raw PAN or CVV. Our logs are access-controlled, encrypted, and contain no card data.
notes: False-positive test (compliant). Must find 3.5 and judge it SATISFIED via tokenization. WATCH FOR: good-practice/third-party-responsibility chunk (possibly Req 12 service-provider requirements) — bonus, not yet a scored must-have.

scenario: We encrypt stored PANs with AES-256, but the encryption keys are stored in the same database in a plaintext config table.
notes: Tests key-management requirement (3.6.1). Encryption is undermined by co-located plaintext keys.

scenario: Our ops team shares a single root login to access servers in the cardholder data environment. There are no individual user accounts.
notes: Access/auth domain (outside the Req 3 cluster). Unique IDs required (8.2.1); shared/generic accounts prohibited (8.2.2).

scenario: Engineers access the cardholder data environment remotely using only username and password. We are rolling out MFA next quarter.
notes: MFA controls: 8.4.2 (MFA into the CDE), 8.4.3 (MFA for remote access from outside the network), 8.5 (MFA systems configured to prevent misuse). 8.4.2 was best-practice until 31 March 2025 and is now required. 'Next quarter' does not excuse it.

scenario: We store only the first-6/last-4 truncated PAN for reconciliation, never the full PAN or CVV, in an encrypted store with role-based access and audit logging.
notes: Second compliant case. Truncation is an explicitly permitted protection method; must judge SATISFIED. Watch for 3.4 (truncation) retrieval.

scenario: During incident debugging we temporarily enable verbose logging that captures full track data from card swipes for 48 hours, then purge it.
notes: Full track data is SAD and must not be stored (3.3.1, 3.3.1.1). 'Temporary' and 'then purged' do not make storage permissible.
